extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, patent owners, and third-party requesters preparing USPTO ex parte reexamination requests
extracted.subtask_description: Preparing and filing a request for ex parte reexamination under 37 CFR 1.510 and related MPEP guidance, including required elements, evidentiary and formatting rules, and strategic showing of a substantial new question of patentability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of fee for requesting ex parte reexamination (37 CFR 1.510(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: The request must be accompanied by the fee for requesting reexamination set in § 1.20(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The entire fee required under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(1) must be paid to obtain a filing date. If the request is filed by the patent owner and includes a proposed amendment under 37 CFR 1.530, excess claims fees under 37 CFR 1.20(c)(3) and (c)(4) may apply. Different filing fees exist for large entity, small entity, and micro entity; to pay reduced small/micro entity fees the requester must affirmatively state eligibility. A third-party requester cannot establish micro entity status. If the fee is missing, requester will be notified and given an opportunity to complete; failure to comply will result in no filing date and possible placement of the papers in the patent file as a citation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required statement pointing out each substantial new question of patentability (37 CFR 1.510(b)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A statement pointing out each substantial new question (SNQ) of patentability based on prior patents and printed publications must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The statement should clearly point out what the requester considers to be the SNQ that would warrant reexamination and must explain how the cited prior art raises that SNQ. It must demonstrate that the patent or printed publication presents a new, non-cumulative technological teaching not previously considered in prosecution or earlier proceedings. It is not sufficient merely to propose rejections; the request must show how questions raised are substantially different from those in the earlier examination. Old art previously considered by the Office may raise an SNQ only if presented/viewed in a new light or different way with a material new argument or interpretation. Clarification of obviousness law (e.g., KSR) alone, without presenting art in a new light, will not raise an SNQ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identification of every claim and detailed explanation applying prior art (37 CFR 1.510(b)(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: An identification of every claim for which reexamination is requested and a detailed explanation of the pertinency and manner of applying the cited prior art to every such claim is required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The request must apply all cited prior art to each claim for which reexamination is requested, explaining how the cited documents meet or teach the claim limitations to establish the identified SNQ or proposed ground of rejection. If relying on any patent owner statement under § 1.501(a)(2), the request must explain how that statement is used to determine claim meaning in connection with the prior art. The detailed explanation should be limitation-by-limitation (claim charts are recommended). Do not lump claims, documents, or combinations together without separate explanations. For obviousness rejections, provide at least one basis for combining references and explain why the claim would have been obvious over that combination (preferably quoting pertinent teachings with page/column/line/figure citations). Examples of inappropriate language (e.g., using 'and/or', lumping multiple references without specific mappings) are provided and should be avoided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copies of every patent or printed publication relied upon and translations (37 CFR 1.510(b)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of every patent or printed publication relied upon or referred to must be submitted, with English translations of necessary and pertinent parts of non-English documents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All cited patents/printed publications must be provided so examiners can fully consider them. Copies must be legible when scanned into the Image File Wrapper; illegible copies are deemed not provided and will be identified in a Notice of Failure to Comply. An English language translation (not merely a summary or abstract) of the necessary portions of non-English documents is required. It is helpful to include prior art considered during earlier prosecution so the Office can compare old and new art to determine if an SNQ exists. Color photographs may be retained as artifacts if legible; otherwise the copy is defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Copy of the entire patent for which reexamination is requested (37 CFR 1.510(b)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: A copy of the entire patent including the front face, drawings, and specification/claims (in double column format) and any disclaimer/certificate/correction must be supplied, with each page plainly written on only one side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The printed patent can be used to provide abstract, drawings, specification, and claims for the request; reproduce the printed patent on one side of paper only (two-sided copies are not proper). Any disclaimers, certificates of correction, or reexamination certificates that are part of the patent must be supplied to provide the complete patent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification of service on the patent owner (37 CFR 1.510(b)(5))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification that a copy of the request filed by a person other than the patent owner has been served in its entirety on the patent owner at the address provided in § 1.33(c) is required, including the name and address of the party served.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service was not possible after reasonable effort, a duplicate copy must be supplied to the Office together with a cover letter explaining the effort and why unsuccessful; clearly mark such filings (e.g., 'Duplicate Copy of Request... When Service on the Patent Owner Was Not Possible') to avoid fee mischarging. The certification must set forth the name and address used in serving the patent owner. Failure to serve may limit the requester's ability to participate later in the proceeding.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification regarding estoppel (37 CFR 1.510(b)(6))
rubrics_metrics.description: A certification by the third-party requester that estoppel provisions of 35 U.S.C. 315(e)(1) or 325(e)(1) do not prohibit filing the ex parte reexamination request must be included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This certifies that inter partes review or post-grant review estoppel does not bar the requester from filing reexamination. The rules do not require identification of the real party in interest on filing; an anonymous real party in interest may use a registered practitioner to file, and the practitioner certifies non-estoppel. An individual filing on his own behalf cannot remain anonymous because he must sign the certification. 37 CFR 11.18 certification obligations apply to practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Filing date obtained only when all requirements satisfied (37 CFR 1.510(c)/(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The filing date of the request is the date on which the request satisfies all requirements of the section; incomplete requests generally receive notice and opportunity to complete.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests that fail to meet all requirements will not be granted a filing date unless corrected within the specified time; if defects are not cured, request will be considered incomplete and may be placed in the patent file as a prior art citation if it meets § 1.501 citation requirements. Refunds may be available if request is denied or vacated, or if found incomplete and not cured, under 37 CFR 1.26.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on submitting an application data sheet (ADS) in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: An application data sheet (ADS) under 37 CFR 1.76 cannot be submitted in a reexamination proceeding since a reexamination proceeding is not an 'application.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not include an ADS with reexamination filings; use the recommended transmittal forms (e.g., PTO/SB/57) instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Form PTO/SB/57 recommended (transmittal/cover sheet)
rubrics_metrics.description: Form PTO/SB/57 is helpful as the transmittal form and cover sheet for a request for reexamination; its use is encouraged but not required by law or rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Using PTO/SB/57 can assist in organizing the request and asserting small entity status (checkbox), but failure to use the form does not invalidate the request so long as the statutory and regulatory requirements are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of permissible bases: prior patents and printed publications only
rubrics_metrics.description: Substantial new questions of patentability must be based on patents and printed publications; questions based on public use, on sale, conduct by parties, 35 U.S.C. 101, 112, inventorship, etc., should not be included and will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A prior art patent or printed publication cannot be used merely as evidence of alleged public use, on sale, or insufficiency of disclosure — it must be applied directly to claim grounds under 35 U.S.C. 102/103 or relate to application of other patents/printed publications. Admissions and affidavits may be used in limited circumstances (see separate rubric entries).

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for what constitutes a 'substantial new question of patentability' (SNQ)
rubrics_metrics.description: An SNQ exists when a patent or printed publication presents a new, non-cumulative technological teaching not previously considered and discussed on the record during prosecution or earlier proceedings, or when old art is presented in a materially new light or with a new analysis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The requester must show how the questions of patentability raised are substantially different from those raised in previous examination. Presentation of old art under a new interpretation or material new argument may suffice. Legal changes such as KSR's clarification of obviousness do not by themselves create an SNQ unless the art is presented in a new light. The statutory requirement for an SNQ remains even when prior art was previously cited to the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Completeness of the explanation applying prior art (I. EXPLANATION MUST BE COMPLETE)
rubrics_metrics.description: The mere citation of new patents/printed publications without explanation does not comply with 37 CFR 1.510(b)(2); requester must present an explanation of how the cited references are applied to all claims considered to merit reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide a claim-by-claim application of each cited reference (claim charts recommended), explaining how each reference or combination is used. Do not include background references not used to support an SNQ. Examples of inappropriate phrasing and appropriate phrasing are provided to clarify acceptable specificity. If the request is nonetheless readily understood, it may be accepted despite certain deficiencies, but lack of explanation will ordinarily trigger a Notice of Failure to Comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of Notices of Failure to Comply and available responses
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office issues a 'Notice of Failure to Comply with Ex Parte Reexamination Request Filing Requirements' identifying documents/combinations/claims lacking explanation, the requester may respond by providing separate explanations or explicitly withdrawing those documents/combinations/claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If withdrawing identified items, no explanation is required for withdrawn items. After withdrawal, remaining explanations need only address the non-withdrawn claims and references. Failure to respond appropriately may result in the request being incomplete.

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavits/declarations/other written evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Affidavits or declarations which explain the contents or pertinent dates of prior art patents or printed publications may be considered in reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such evidence can be used to clarify the prior art references' content or dates; see MPEP § 2258 for handling during examination. However, evidence that goes beyond explaining patents/printed publications may be outside reexamination scope.

rubrics_metrics.name: Admissions and use in reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: Admissions by the patent owner of record in the file or in a court record may be utilized in combination with a patent or printed publication; admissions outside the file/court record generally are not admissible from a third party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An admission in the patent file or court record may be used to determine scope/content of prior art in conjunction with patents/printed publications. A third party may not submit admissions made outside the file or court record unless entered into a court record and filed as a copy of a court paper; even then, such admission will not be given weight as an admission for establishing an SNQ apart from patents/printed publications. Admissions must stand on their own; supplemental information further defining an admission is improper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements for showing obviousness grounds (combinations) in the request
rubrics_metrics.description: For proposed obviousness rejections, the requester must provide at least one basis for combining the cited references and explain why the claim(s) would have been obvious over the proposed combination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Preferably quote the pertinent teachings in the references with specific citations (page/column/line/figure). The explanation must not lump references together; if multiple references are combined, explain separately how each reference contributes to the combination and the rationale for the combination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Legibility and format requirements for copies of prior art
rubrics_metrics.description: Copies of prior art must be legible when scanned into the IFW; illegible copies are deemed not provided. Non-English documents require English translations of necessary parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If copies are not legible (or cannot be scanned legibly), the defect will be identified in a Notice of Failure to Comply. English summaries or abstracts of non-English documents are usually insufficient. Color photographs and similar submissions that are legible may be retained in an 'artifact' file and used as such.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entity status assertions and fee consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: To pay small or micro entity fees, requester must affirmatively state eligibility (e.g., check box on PTO/SB/57); third-party requesters cannot assert micro entity status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See 37 CFR 1.27 (small entity) and 1.29 (micro entity) and MPEP §§ 509 for establishing entity status. Refunds of fees may be available under 37 CFR 1.26 if the request is denied, vacated, or found incomplete and not cured, per applicable subsections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limited circumstances where non-patent literature or double patenting issues may be considered
rubrics_metrics.description: While reexamination is limited to patents and printed publications, certain nonstatutory double patenting rejections or 102(g)(2)-type examples may be appropriate in limited circumstances.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples such as In re Lonardo (double patenting) and charted examples for 35 U.S.C. 102(g)(2) are discussed; these are exceptions where reexamination may consider matters tied to patent-to-patent comparisons. Generally, however, matters not based on patents/printed publications should not be presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office discretion to accept imperfect requests if readily understood
rubrics_metrics.description: Even if the request fails to comply with a requirement, the request may be accepted if it is readily understood from the explanation provided how the cited patents/printed publications are applied to the claims at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptance despite defects is discretionary; however, common defects (missing fee, illegible copies, missing explanations) typically trigger Notices of Failure to Comply and require cure to obtain a filing date. Where acceptance occurs, the examiner will consider the provided explanations during examination if reexamination is ordered.
